title: Isolation of Cells from Frozen Human Intestinal Biopsies
author: Oxford HCA
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bcb6isre
materials: 10.Transfer to tubes and run through FACS.

steps.title: Pre‑warm transport and chelation media
steps.instruction: Pre‑warm 10 ml of transport medium and 20 ml of chelation medium per sample in a water bath.

steps.title: Partially thaw frozen biopsies
steps.instruction: Place frozen intestinal biopsies in a 37 °C water bath and thaw until only a little ice remains.

steps.title: Add transport medium to thaw
steps.instruction: Dropwise add 1 ml of the pre‑warmed transport medium to each biopsy to complete thawing.

steps.title: Transfer biopsies to transport conical
steps.instruction: Using a pastette, transfer the biopsies into a conical tube containing the remaining pre‑warmed transport medium.

steps.title: Filter biopsies and wash
steps.instruction: Place a 70 µm filter onto a 50 ml conical tube, transfer the biopsies onto the filter, and wash with 20 ml of cold wash medium.

steps.title: Move biopsies to chelation medium
steps.instruction: Transfer the biopsies into a 50 ml conical tube containing 5 ml of warm chelation medium.

steps.title: Incubate chelation step
steps.instruction: Incubate at 37 °C for 10 minutes in an incubator.

steps.title: Vortex chelation mixture
steps.instruction: Vortex the tube twice for 5–10 seconds each.

steps.title: Collect crypt‑containing supernatant
steps.instruction: Allow biopsies to settle, then use an FCS‑coated pastette to remove the chelation medium (which may contain isolated crypts) and transfer it to a fresh Falcon tube with 5 ml warm chelation medium; return the biopsies to a 37 °C incubator and repeat the incubation, vortex, and collection steps (steps 6‑8).

steps.title: Store chelation fractions
steps.instruction: Keep each collected chelation fraction at 4 °C while proceeding with subsequent isolation steps.

steps.title: Repeat chelation cycles and pool
steps.instruction: Repeat the chelation cycle (steps 6‑9) a total of four times, then pool all crypt‑containing fractions together.

steps.title: Centrifuge pooled crypt suspension
steps.instruction: Spin the pooled crypt suspension at 300 g for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Resuspend in TrypLE/DNase
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 3 ml warm TrypLE Express containing 50 µg ml⁻¹ DNAse (add 75 µl of a 2 mg ml⁻¹ DNAse stock).

steps.title: Digest at 37 °C with shaking
steps.instruction: Incubate for 60 minutes at 37 °C in a shaking incubator set to 220 rpm.

steps.title: Filter through 70 µm strainer
steps.instruction: Pass the digest through a 70 µm cell strainer pre‑coated with FCS into a 50 ml Falcon tube and wash the strainer with 5 ml T5 media.

steps.title: Centrifuge filtrate and wash pellet
steps.instruction: Spin the filtrate at 1500 rpm for 5 minutes, discard supernatant, add 30 ml T5 media to the pellet, and spin again at 1500 rpm for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Reduce supernatant and resuspend
steps.instruction: Very carefully remove supernatant until less than 1 ml remains, then resuspend the pellet in the remaining liquid.

steps.title: Filter through 30 µm strainer
steps.instruction: Pass the suspension through a 30 µm cell strainer pre‑coated with FCS and wash the strainer with 5 ml PBS.

steps.title: Centrifuge and transfer to Eppendorf
steps.instruction: Spin at 1500 rpm for 5 minutes, resuspend the pellet in approximately 1 ml of the remaining PBS, transfer to an Eppendorf tube, and bring the volume up to 1 ml with PBS.

steps.title: Viability stain and count cells
steps.instruction: Take 10 µl of the suspension, mix 1:1 with Trypan blue, and count using a Countess; repeat the count twice and average for viability.

steps.title: Adjust concentration for 10X sequencing
steps.instruction: Spin down in a microcentrifuge at 1500 rpm for 5 minutes, resuspend to a concentration of 2000 cells µl⁻¹ (2 × 10⁶ cells ml⁻¹) using the live count, then re‑check and dilute to 1500 cells µl⁻¹ (1.5 × 10⁶ cells ml⁻¹) with PBS.

steps.title: Transfer cells to 96‑well plate
steps.instruction: Place the cell suspension on ice and transfer epithelial cells to a round‑bottom 96‑well plate.

steps.title: Wash plate before antibody staining
steps.instruction: Spin the plate at 2200 rpm for 2 minutes, discard supernatant, add 200 µl wash buffer, and spin at 2200 rpm for 1 minute; repeat the wash (200 µl, spin 1 minute) once more.

steps.title: Add primary antibodies
steps.instruction: Remove supernatant, add 100 µl FACS buffer, then add 1 µl EpCAM‑PE (1:100), 2 µl CD24‑PE‑CF594 (1:50), and 1 µl CD45‑AF700 (1:100).

steps.title: Incubate antibody staining
steps.instruction: Place the plate in a refrigerator for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Wash after antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Spin the plate at 2200 rpm for 1 minute, discard supernatant, add 200 µl wash buffer, and spin at 2200 rpm for 1 minute; repeat the wash (200 µl, spin 1 minute) once more.

steps.title: Stain with Sytox Green
steps.instruction: Resuspend cells in 300 µl FACS buffer and add 3 µl of a 1:100 diluted Sytox Green solution (prepared by mixing 5 µl Sytox Green with 295 µl FACS buffer, final dilution 1:6000).
